SAMPLING_2026_08_27.issue: GitHub #2 (bczow, S3000XL-VST v1.1, ROM v2.0): 'Trying to sample anything makes the plugin unresponsive. After pressing Go the sampler will not react to pressing any of its buttons.'
SAMPLING_2026_08_27.diagnosis: NOT a plugin bug. Sampling is not implemented in the MAME driver. The A/D (WADCS) is a bare I8255 with no callbacks, referenced by nothing, and an ENTIRE I/O block at 0xC000-0xC03F was unmapped - 261 accesses in the OS ROM go there. The References/mame driver's own TODO list already says 'Recording.'

THE_WAIT.where: 0xEF47D, found by disassembly not by guesswork
THE_WAIT.code: ef47f: mov dx,0C001h/out dx,al (select counter 0) ; ef483: mov dx,0C004h/in ax,dx (position) ; ef487: mov si,[8570h]/cmp ax,si ; ef48d: ja 0EF496h ; ef494: jmp 0EF47Dh
THE_WAIT.target: built at 0xEF3FE as `and bp,3FFh` - the low ten bits of the 32-bit sample address. 0xC002 is written as min(len,0x400)-1 at 0xE00B6. So 0xC004 is a position counter inside a 1024-word transfer page.
THE_WAIT.why_it_hangs: 0xC004 unmapped -> reads 0 -> the comparison never passes -> the firmware waits forever, shows 0%, and never reaches its panel scan, so F8/ABORT is dead.

SAMPLING_2026_08_27.A_SECOND_SPINNER_NOT_THE_CAUSE: 0xEEBD9 spins on bit 7 of I/O 0x01C0 (also unmapped) before writing a byte to the WADCS at 0x00C0. It is gated by `test byte ptr [8490h],1` at 0xEEBD2 and that flag is clear on our machine, so the routine returns immediately. Ruled out by evidence, not assumed.
METHOD_NOTE_TWO_OF_MY_OWN_INSTRUMENTS_WE: A raw byte scan of the ROM for in/out opcodes was NOISE and was discarded: control windows with NOTHING mapped scored 525 and 36 hits against 74 for the real one, with 256 expected by chance.
The disassembly analyser then missed every hit because unidasm prints immediates with UPPERCASE hex (1C0h) and the regex was lowercase-only.
Both were caught by controls BEFORE anything was reported. Same class as the U517 defect in the Virus work: a search that matches the wrong column.

IS_IT_ALREADY_IMPLEMENTED_IN_MAME.s3000xl: NO. The A/D is `I8255(config, m_wadcs);` - a bare 8255 with zero callbacks, referenced by no handler anywhere in the file, and no DMA request line feeds it. The driver's own TODO list says 'Recording.' Nothing to reuse.
IS_IT_ALREADY_IMPLEMENTED_IN_MAME.s1000: YES, but a DIFFERENT ARCHITECTURE, and Thor was right to press on this. The S1000 has: a custom L6009 gate array supplying a real sample clock via sample_clock_cb(); TWO adc16 devices, one per channel; TWO DMA channels (0 and 1), one per channel; and therefore NO L/R INTERLEAVE AT ALL.
IS_IT_ALREADY_IMPLEMENTED_IN_MAME.why_it_matters: The S1000 pattern transfers only partially, and the part it does NOT cover - a single serial converter interleaving L and R down one DMA channel - is exactly the part that cost this session five rounds. Copying the shape of s1000.cpp was right for the wiring and useless for the hard problem.

THE_INPUT_PATH_AS_ESTABLISHED: 1. Analog In PCB L6036A501B - jacks J201/J202 -> M5220P/M5220L op-amps -> W201 -> main PCB P16 (AINL/AINR). PURE ANALOG, nothing to emulate.

2. IC50 AK5339-VP - 16-bit dual A/D, 64fs oversampling with decimation filter. SERIAL output: SDATA pin 16, SCLK pin 15, L/R pin 14, CLK IN pin 23, APD/DPD power-down. The L/R pin is an OUTPUT of the converter, so the channel of each word is defined by the converter and cannot drift.
3. IC41 HD74HC244P - 3-state buffer between the PALs and the converter (FSYNC, SCLK, ADLR, SDATA, ICLKD).
4. IC29 PALCE16V8Q (L6039D) - serial clock and framing: in BTCK, LRWCK, SRCLK, SER; out PD, FSYNC, SCLK, BLRWCK, ADLR, L_OUT, SDATA, 22/44.
5. IC30 PALCE20V8Q (L6039B) - THE DMA REQUEST GENERATOR: in SDLRD, WADCS, BTCK, TORD, DAK2, 384FS, FBSY, TOUT1, D0/D1, A1; out LDMA, RDMA, 22/44, YMLR, OPDETN, ICLKD, BBTCK, DMRQ2, SIOPG.
6. V53 DMA channel 2. WADCS is a CHIP SELECT from the HD74HC154 decoder (seen on the S2000 main-board page), not a data path - which is why the 8255 was never the answer.
SAMPLING_SESSION_2026_08_27.STILL_UNKNOWN_AND_WHAT_WOULD_SETTLE_IT: How DMRQ2 relates to LDMA/RDMA and DAK2 inside IC30 - specifically whether the PAL asserts one request per WORD or per FRAME, and what clears it. Three rounds have been spent correcting my model of that handshake instead of reading the real one. The page showing IC29/IC30 with every pin and the nets running to the V53 is the source that ends the guessing.
SAMPLING_SESSION_2026_08_27.TRANSPORT_NOW_MEASURED_CORRECT: ADC-DMA 44100 words per 0.5000 s = 88200 words/s = 44100 stereo frames/s exactly; ADC-FIFO starved 0; host ring DROPPED 0; emulation ratio 0.987-1.016 around unity. Every rate in the chain agrees. The remaining distortion is therefore NOT transport.
WHAT_WAS_FIXED_AND_WHY: DMA channel 2 wired at all - it was connected to nothing, and the firmware waited on a transfer that could never arrive. THAT was the freeze.
OSD sound_stream_source_open returned 0, which means REFUSED, so MAME never opened an input stream.
The JUCE input bus shipped default-off, so processBlock never pushed a sample however the host was wired.
The OSD node declared no channel positions, so MAME's position-based matcher built zero mixing steps and pulled nothing, silently.
adc16::read() forced a full MAME stream update 88200 times a second and cost 61 per cent of real time; replaced by a block-fed device pulled at 4 kHz into a FIFO.
Starvation returned silence, putting a step to zero into the waveform on every underrun; a converter's output register HOLDS its last conversion, so it now holds.
SAMPLING_SESSION_2026_08_27.MY_OWN_INSTRUMENT_FAILURES_THIS_SESSION: FIVE, all the same class - an instrument that could not report the state it was built to detect: a meter that printed only when frames arrived and so said nothing when none did; a starvation counter never printed; a drop counter never printed; a format string that lost its peak arguments; and a build chain where two scripts in one command silently skipped the second while returning exit code 0. Rule reinforced: check the ARTEFACT, never the exit code, and make every instrument able to report absence.

SAMPLING_SESSION_2026_08_28.headline: The recording works and is wrong in one specific way: the A/D DMA fills a 4096-word ring at $0091B0 and wraps every 92.9 ms, and the firmware's copy-out is not synchronised to that wrap. The audio is spliced on a 4468-sample grid, 9.87 Hz, about 141 samples lost or re-recorded each time.
MEASURED_FACTS: THE BUFFER: ADC-WRAP shows the DMA destination returning to $0091B0 every 4096 words, forty consecutive times with no deviation. One contiguous ring, two bytes per word, at 44100 words/s that is 92.9 ms.

ONE WORD IS ONE FRAME on this path, measured absolutely with a per-frame counter fed to the DMA instead of the microphone: playback gain 13128/65532 = 0.2003, measured slope 0.8011 units/sample, ratio 4.00 which is exactly the ramp's step. Not inferred from a rate this code imposes.
THE MACHINE'S OWN SCREEN: RECORD STEREO, tim 1.00s = 88200. Two words per frame collected into one place.
THE SPLICE GRID: 4468 samples median, identical on both channels, 47 and 46 events in a 5-second capture. About 141 samples missing per splice, median 141.1 left and 141.0 right over 28 events each.
THE CHANNEL SKEW is a beat, not a new fault: +395 samples in one run, -398 in the next. Same magnitude, opposite sign.
THE TRANSPORT IS CLEAN END TO END: 150821 consecutive DMA words with no break past 2 ms; plugin ring DROPPED=0, ratio 0.998; ADC FIFO starved=0 with drops only in the second after a recording ends.
THE RECORDING LENGTH IS CORRECT - Thor's 5-second setting yields 5 seconds of audio. The doubled elapsed time is the WAVEFORM DRAWING, not a starved transfer.

THE FREEZE NEEDS A SIGNAL: with nothing on the input, RECORD then GO does not freeze and abort works. With a signal the recording runs and is audible through the monitor, but the waveform never draws and abort no longer stops it. The machine itself keeps running - ADC-RATE reports 44100 words/s for twenty more seconds after the panel stops responding.
RETRACTED_THIS_SESSION: SAMPLING 39's claim that 44100 words/s proved one word per frame. DREQ is only raised when the FIFO holds a frame and the FIFO fills at 44100/s, so that rate is the CEILING THIS CODE IMPOSES. starved=0 is empty for the same reason. The conclusion happened to be right; the reasoning was circular.

SAMPLING 46's claim that the A/D never reaches terminal count. The attribution required machine().time() to EQUAL the channel-2 DACK timestamp, and am9517a.cpp asserts EOP in STATE_S3 while set_dack() runs in STATE_S2 - they can never be equal, so every EOP was filtered out and the silence was read as absence. end_of_process() only reloads the base address under MODE_AUTOINITIALIZE, and the measured wrap to $0091B0 IS that reload, so the terminal count has been arriving all along.
SAMPLING 41's reading of the doubled elapsed time as a transfer starved to half rate.

SAMPLING_SESSION_2026_08_29.status: Phase one closed: the recording path is DIAGNOSED, not fixed. Audio arrives, the pitch is right, the length is right, and the stored content is wrong in one specific, measured way.
THE_MACHINE_AS_MEASURED: The A/D DMA fills a 4096-word ring at $0091B0. The firmware ARMS IT ITSELF at GO - reg 04/05/06 = B0/91/00, reg 02/03 = FF/0F, reg 0A = 55 - so word mode, into memory, autoinitialise, and the ring starts at zero phase.

Terminal count fires every 4096 words, 92.9 ms, confirmed by ADC-EOP and ADC-WRAP landing in the same microsecond forty times over. out_eop_cb reaches only the floppy's TC merger, so nothing tells the firmware.
The firmware tracks the ring by POLLING THE DMA'S CURRENT ADDRESS - registers 04h/05h, 223870 times a second, never the count and never the status.

Its routine at 0271B0h: out C001h,2 / in ax,C004h / sub ax,91B0h / sub ax,bx / modulo 2000h / jz re-read / sub ax,800h, answer in CF. Every quantity a BYTE offset, which settles the address-increment question from the firmware's own arithmetic: two bytes per word.
Its caller at 027184h advances a 32-bit value at [7904] (DS=0, so linear 007904h) and loops call-poll / copy / repeat until the difference falls below 800h.

0270C6h is a plain rep movsw from the ring to 3A60:62AA - no interpolation. And it copies NOTHING during a recording: DX is 0000h, so CX is zero, and a write tap on its destination at linear 408AAh never fired once. That routine walks the ring without storing - most likely the waveform display.

THE RECORD STORE IS ON DMA CHANNEL 3, into the L7A1045's sample memory. Measured there, in the second the A/D delivered 44100 words: 529200 stored, TWELVE TIMES as many, as an unbroken +1 sequence - 529071 of 529200, zero repeats - with 129 discontinuities, one per 4009 words against a ring of 4096.
RATE-ADV: the read position advances 2.007 bytes per DMA word - locked. The read side is correct.

TOUT1 runs at 44199 Hz constantly and gates IC30's outputs, DMRQ2 among them. The DACK is ACTIVE LOW, measured 88189 zeros against 44100 words and 1058411 ones - this driver had it backwards since the channel was first wired, and that is fixed.
WHAT_IS_FIXED_AND_KEPT: DMA channel 2 wired at all - the original freeze of GitHub issue #2.
The DACK polarity, settled by arithmetic that admits no other reading.
One word per frame on this path, measured absolutely with a per-frame counter: playback gain 0.2003, slope 0.8011, ratio exactly 4.00 against a ramp stepping 4.
RULED_OUT_BY_MEASUREMENT: The A/D transfer cannot be rate-limited. Four builds paced it - from TOUT1, from the converter's clock, and twice from a due time - and all four stopped the machine at RECORD, twice with the input meter blank. It must be free to burst.
The burst window is not the cause: at 11025 Hz the gap is 68 us instead of 193 and the seams did not move.
The µPD71071 address-increment analogy: refuted by the firmware's own byte arithmetic.
The rate-conversion increment: refuted, the copy is a block move.

The whole-space write tap and the 156453-lines-a-second log: both took the emulation below real time and produced a ten-to-thirty-second waveform draw that I read as a machine defect. Thor caught it by remembering it had been fine.
SAMPLING_SESSION_2026_08_29.NEXT: Find why the store on channel 3 writes twelve words for every one the converter delivers. The read side is locked and the ring is correct, so the multiplication happens at or after the store. That is one loop with one exit condition.
SAMPLING_SESSION_2026_08_29.MY_RETRACTIONS_THIS_SESSION: NINE, and one of those was itself withdrawn. The rule that would have caught all of them is now first on the list - before believing a measurement, ask WHAT READING WOULD HAVE BEEN IMPOSSIBLE. If none, it is not a measurement.

SAMPLING_SOLVED_2026_08_29.GOLDEN_COMMIT: mame@2bb825d8 (fix at ecf41001, confirmed at fe077bea) - clean mono recording, verified at the storage point and by ear
SAMPLING_SOLVED_2026_08_29.THE_FAULT_IN_ONE_SENTENCE: The L7A1045's DMA request timer was set to 64 ticks of a 33.8688 MHz clock - 529200 requests a second - where the sample period is 768 ticks, so the sound chip asked the CPU for a word TWELVE times per sample and the machine stored twelve times what the converter delivered.
SAMPLING_SOLVED_2026_08_29.THE_FIX: l7a1045_l6028_dsp_a.cpp, dma_timer: attotime::from_ticks(64, clock()) -> from_ticks(768, clock()). One request per sample period, 44100 a second, which is what the A/D delivers.
SAMPLING_SOLVED_2026_08_29.WHY_THE_64_WAS_THERE: The line's comment read '8x the sample period'. That eight is the OUTPUT OVERSAMPLING of the D/A - the S3200 block diagram shows it as IC12, 'OVER SAMPLING (8X) DIGITAL FILTER (20BIT)', feeding two 20-bit DACs. A property of the playback path used to pace an INPUT transfer, and it did not even match its own comment: 8x would be 96 ticks, the code asked for 64. Thor identified the eight.

after:  SAMPLE-STORE 44100 words/s, step+1 44100 (100.0%), repeat 0, jump 0, worst 0
DSP-DREQ3 rose 44100 times against 44099 words stored - one word per request, the DMA controller was always faultless

SAMPLING_SOLVED_2026_08_29.EVERY_SYMPTOM_CAME_FROM_THAT_ONE_INTEGER: the 4468-sample splice grid, the seams one ring long, the repeated content, the copy loop at 0271A3 whose exit condition could never be reached, and the freeze.
SAMPLING_SOLVED_2026_08_29.WHAT_MADE_IT_FINDABLE: A per-frame counter fed to the converter instead of audio. SAMPLING_STATE_2026_08_29_EVENING.headline: TWO SEPARATE FAULTS, both located. The RECORDING ITSELF IS CORRECT - measured. The MEMORY CORRUPTION is a firmware copy loop that never exits, and it was present in every build including the one called golden.

FAULT_1_RATE_SOLVED.what: l7a1045_l6028_dsp_a.cpp's DMA request timer used from_ticks(64, clock()) = 529200/s where the sample period is 768 ticks, so the chip asked twelve times per sample and the machine stored twelve times what arrived.
FAULT_1_RATE_SOLVED.proof: SAMPLE-STORE 44100 words, step+1 100.0%, repeat 0, jump 0. DMA-DST 44100 words, contiguous 44099 (100.0%), jumps 0, span 88198 bytes = 44099 x 2. The firmware's aim is perfect.
FAULT_1_RATE_SOLVED.the_8x: The old comment said '8x the sample period'. That eight is the OUTPUT oversampling of the D/A - S3200 block diagram IC12, 'OVER SAMPLING (8X) DIGITAL FILTER (20BIT)' feeding two 20-bit DACs. Thor identified it. A playback property used to pace an input transfer.
FAULT_1_RATE_SOLVED.cost: Sample LOADING is paced by the same timer and is now twelve times slower. Also the MONITOR goes silent during recording in this build, where it sounded in about nine of ten earlier ones - so the monitor travels the same DMA and 768 is right for the recording but wrong for the device as a whole.

FAULT_2_MEMORY_CORRUPTION_OPEN.what: The transfer never ends. For a ONE SECOND recording the destination marches through sample memory - 032710, 047F96, 0563EA, 020000, 035888, 04B7F8, 061080, 076908, 08C190, 0A1A18, 0B72A0 - roughly 600 KB in ten seconds, paving every sample already loaded. That is why the built-in waveforms turn sawtooth-like: they sit at fixed addresses.
FAULT_2_MEMORY_CORRUPTION_OPEN.not_the_dma: mode 49h has bit 4 clear, so NO autoinitialise, and end_of_process() masks the channel. count reaching FFFFFFFFh is only the post-decrement remainder after termination. The controller behaves.
FAULT_2_MEMORY_CORRUPTION_OPEN.it_is_the_firmware_loop: The firmware RE-ARMS channel 3 block after block - source 0091B0h, count 07FFh, 2048 words, 800h bytes, exactly the block size in its own routine at 0271A3h - and far more often than the ~21 arms a one-second recording needs. 803 register writes in one run.
FAULT_2_MEMORY_CORRUPTION_OPEN.why_it_cannot_exit: The loop exits when avail falls below 800h. avail is the A/D ring pointer minus BX, and BX is NOT updated inside the loop, so in this model it can only grow. The firmware is scripture and exits on real hardware, so something that moves on the board does not move here.
FAULT_2_MEMORY_CORRUPTION_OPEN.present_in_golden: Thor confirms the corruption was there in mame@2bb825d8 too. It is independent of the twelve, and the SAMPLING 91 prediction that the correct rate would clear it is withdrawn.

RULED_OUT_BY_MEASUREMENT: The destination pointer is NOT wrong - 100 per cent contiguous, zero jumps. The shared-voice-pointer suspicion of SAMPLING 90 is finished, and that change crashed the machine on start: Thor corrected both its premises - during a recording only the MONITOR sounds, and the recording always goes to the SELECTED SAMPLE's location, so voice 0's start is the intended destination, not a collision.

The DMA request line cannot be paced from our side. Three attempts - SAMPLING 57 from TOUT1, 60/61/68 from a clock and a due time on channel 2, and 91 on channel 3 - and every one degraded the machine: crashes, blank input meter, a late monitor, a capture falling out of time. THE REQUEST IS NOT A KNOB.
SAMPLING_STATE_2026_08_29_EVENING.NEXT: DMA3-ARM prints BX, the A/D ring offset and the resulting avail at every arm. If avail falls arm by arm the loop converges and the trouble is elsewhere; if it is flat or rising, this is the runaway and the question becomes what should have moved.

CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.measured: run_125, one run containing mono, stereo, mono in that order, logging EVERY control-word write to the L7A1045: MONO writes CTRL 0150 and STEREO writes CTRL 0158, to the same channels 16 and 23, with every other bit identical. One bit: 0x08, bit 3.

windows.MONO 116.1-118.3: CTRL 0150 again - the bit is NOT persistent

CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.the_gap: Bit 3 is UNMODELLED. The device knows only CONTROL_DMA_START (6) and CONTROL_KEY_ON (8); bit 3 is one of the '?' bits in the register-4 documentation. So the machine states something about the transfer and we silently drop it - the class of defect this project already named: an unmodelled register is not neutral.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.what_it_is_not: Not the stereo-pair heuristic added for the MPC3000: that triggers on complementary hard-panned volumes and pairs ch with ch^2, but here the pair is 16 and 23, which is not a ^2 pair, and the firmware issues its own key-on for each. The heuristic does not fire on this machine.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.what_it_does_not_explain_yet: The monitor becoming audible after one stereo recording and STAYING audible. Bit 3 is not persistent - the later mono recordings write 0150 again - so whatever persists is something else that the stereo pass leaves behind.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.leading_hypothesis: Bit 3 tells the chip the DMA transfer it is about to service is STEREO, i.e. the chip itself de-interleaves the incoming stream across the two voices. That would be the missing piece, and it sits exactly where every measurement has been pointing: downstream of the converter, on the sound chip, not in the word rate or the word order.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.status: MEASURED. Nothing modelled on it yet.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.tested_and_reverted: SAMPLING 126 read bit 3 as 'split the DMA words across two destinations, voice 0 and voice 1'. THE PLUGIN FROZE. Reverted (mame@6bb3378c). So voice 1's pointer is not a valid second destination - writing there stops the machine - and bit 3 does NOT mean that.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.what_survives: The measurement itself: mono writes CTRL 0150 and stereo writes CTRL 0158, same channels, one bit apart, and bit 3 is unmodelled. That stands. Only the meaning I attached to it was wrong.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.next_reading_to_consider: Bit 3 is written together with KEY_ON (0x0158 = key_on | dma_start | bit4 | bit3) and it goes to BOTH voices of the pair, ch16 and ch23. So it may be a PER-VOICE flag meaning 'this voice is one half of a stereo pair' - a playback property - rather than anything about the DMA transfer. Not tested, and not to be built on without evidence.
CONTROL_BIT3_IS_THE_STEREO_BIT_2026_08_3.cost_so_far: Five builds have now tried to make stereo work by changing what we send or where it goes - 111, 112, 119, 122, 126 - and all five were reverted. Mono has survived every one of them intact, which is the one thing the gating has reliably delivered.

R_REGION_IS_FED_BUT_ONLY_ONE_BLOCK_2026_.reading: The firmware copies from a ring half while enough data is available there and stops when it is not - the avail >= 0x800 test in its own loop. Our A/D fills the ring linearly with left words only, so the UPPER half never accumulates anything new and the copy stops after a single block. That is consistent with the upper half being the right channel's place, which is where the two end-of-recording sources 0091B0 and 00A1B0 already pointed.
R_REGION_IS_FED_BUT_ONLY_ONE_BLOCK_2026_.what_it_does_not_settle: How the hardware gets the right channel into the upper half. One arm of DMA channel 2 at 0091B0, mode-independent, is all the firmware does - measured in SAMPLING 116. Delivering the pair interleaved has been tried four times and fails.

RING_IS_ONE_LINEAR_BUFFER_2026_08_30.tested: SAMPLING 128 placed the right word into the ring's upper half at the same relative position as the left, leaving the left path byte-for-byte untouched. Thor: the right channel is still only the spike. Reverted (mame@f735184e).
RING_IS_ONE_LINEAR_BUFFER_2026_08_30.what_it_falsifies: THE WHOLE 'two halves = two channels' READING, mine, built over several rounds. The firmware's own position routine at 0271B0 reads the DMA current address, subtracts 0x91B0, and takes it MODULO 0x2000 - it treats the ring as ONE linear 8192-byte buffer. 0091B0 and 00A1B0 are two BLOCK BOUNDARIES inside it, not two channel areas.
RING_IS_ONE_LINEAR_BUFFER_2026_08_30.why_00A1B0_only_appears_in_stereo: Not because it is the right channel's home. Because a stereo recording has MORE DATA PENDING at the end, so the closing flush spans two 2048-word blocks instead of one. Quantity, not channel. This also explains the single 2048-word block the -R region receives, which Thor hears as one transient spike.
RING_IS_ONE_LINEAR_BUFFER_2026_08_30.consequence: The stereo difference is NOT in the ring. It is not in the word rate, the word order, the destination half, or the voice split - all tested and reverted. What is left are the two FLAGS: $00C0 bit 4 and the L7A1045 control bit 3, both measured, both unmodelled.
RING_IS_ONE_LINEAR_BUFFER_2026_08_30.module_maturity_check: Thor's method: upd71071/v5x_dmau is used by fmtowns, apxen, s900, future32 and an Acorn podule - broadly exercised, so unlikely to hold a fault of ours, and everything we put there is logging. The l7a1045 is used only by mpc2000, mpc3000, s3000 and SNK Hyper NeoGeo 64, and the HNG64 loads samples without ever recording - so this chip's DMA-IN path is exercised by nobody but us. Consistent with SAMPLING 87 finding a real upstream defect exactly there.

STEREO_RECORDING_WORKS_2026_09_13.fix: SAMPLING 149 (mame@38158a24). The second destination of the bit-3 split is the firmware's own [7914:7912] taken UNSHIFTED. SAMPLING 148 had shifted it right by one to 'convert to words' - a guess about a unit, wrong in the wrong direction.
STEREO_RECORDING_WORKS_2026_09_13.derivation: The arm routine at 26177 packs the destination into the chip's 48-bit register layout with ROR 4: out 86 = (ror(hi,4) & 001F) | 0100 gives a[23:20] = hi[7:4]; out 82 = ror(lo,4) & F000 gives a[3:0] = lo[3:0]; out 84 = (ror(lo,4) & 0FFF) | (ror(hi,4) & F000) gives a[15:4] = lo[15:4] and a[19:16] = hi[3:0]. Reassembled: a[23:0] = D[23:0]. The ROR is PACKING, not conversion.
STEREO_RECORDING_WORKS_2026_09_13.cross_check: Independent, from data already recorded: for the -L transfer BLOCKREQ measured [7772]=0400 [7774]=0002, so D = 020400, and DMA-BURST - which prints m_voice[0].start - reported dest 020400 for that same transfer. Identical, no shift between them. That is what makes this a derivation rather than a second guess.

MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.verdict: Thor: OUT1-8 -> DAW1-8 perfect, the stuttering is gone. Multi out is DONE.
MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.what_was_already_there: The emulation side was finished and nobody had noticed. l7a1045 allocates TEN outputs (L6028_LEFT, L6028_RIGHT, L6028_OUT0..OUT7) and already wrote the discrete ones with stream.add_int(2 + channel_remap[dest], ...). Missing was only the driver: a two-channel speaker with the stereo pair routed, so eight outputs were computed every sample and thrown away.
MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.layout: Eight MONO buses plus the main stereo pair, ten in all - Thor's call, and his reason: sending drums out separately would be odd with the kick on the right of one stereo channel and the open hat on the left. The machine has eight separate jacks.
MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.jack_order: MEASURED END TO END, not derived. Thor stepped indiv: 1..8 and read where each came out. The machine's OUT n arrives on L6028_OUT [4,6,5,7,0,2,1,3], so routing those to indiv channels 0..7 puts OUT n on DAW n. If channel_remap or the firmware's dest numbering ever changes, RE-MEASURE with the same eight-step test rather than reasoning about it.
MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.routing_settled_by_three_sources: Anything sent to an individual output is ALSO summed to the stereo pair. (1) the machine's own program page shows 'stereo level: 99' and 'indiv: 8 lev:50' as two live parameters; (2) the device models exactly that - l_volume/r_volume for the pair, send_level for the send; (3) a Sound On Sound post: 'Anything assigned to the individual outputs are summed and always appear at the stereo outputs as well. It has ever been thus since the S900/1000.' Removing a sound from the main is the user's choice of stereo level, not a routing mode. Thor expected the opposite and the evidence corrected us both.
MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.the_mix_map_is_derived: The plugin computes stride and offsets at runtime by walking speaker_device_enumerator and matching the speaker TAG, exactly as emu/sound.cpp lays the record buffer out. The old hardcoded 'stride 3, ch0 = floppy' was a real measurement that silently expired the moment a speaker was added. Measured after the change: MIXMAP stride=11 main=1 indiv=3.
MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.floppy_speaker: enable_sound(false) does NOT remove it - floppy_image_device::device_add_mconfig creates the speaker unconditionally, so the stride is 11 and not the 10 I expected. Removing it would mean editing floppy.cpp, which hundreds of drivers use. It stays as one silent channel, handled by the derived map. Deriving is what caught this; a hardcoded stride would have shifted every channel.
MULTIOUT_DONE_2026_09_13.THE_STUTTER_WAS_THE_PROBES: FIFTH time in this project that an instrument of mine was noticed by ear. I had a plausible and WRONG theory - that the mix stride going from 3 to 11 was the cost - and had I acted on it I would have spent the next round making the indiv speaker optional, solving a problem that did not exist. Removing the 64 MAME logerror calls and the plugin's per-frame peak meter fixed it. The rule stands and has now cost five rounds: an instrument on an always-running path is itself an intervention.
